EGAPx overview ==============
EGAPx is the publicly accessible version of the NCBI `Eukaryotic Genome Annotation Pipeline <https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/refseq/annotation_euk/process/>`_.
EGAPx takes an assembly FASTA file, the taxonomy ID (taxid) of the organism, and RNA sequencing data. It automatically chooses protein sets and HMM models based on the taxid. The pipeline runs ``miniprot`` or ``ProSplign`` to align protein sequences, ``STAR`` to align short RNA-seq reads, and ``minimap2`` to align long RNA-seq reads to the assembly. Protein and RNA-seq alignments are passed to ``Gnomon`` for gene prediction: short alignments are chained into putative gene models, which are then supplemented by *ab initio* predictions based on HMM models. Functional annotation is added based on the type and quality of each model and orthology information. Optionally, noncoding RNAs (tRNAs, rRNAs, snoRNAs and snRNAs) can be predicted with ``tRNAscan`` and ``cmsearch``. EGAPx produces the annotation in ASN.1 format (for GenBank submission) and GFF3/GTF formats.
.. image:: $PATH_TO_IMAGES/EGAPx.diagram.png
**Supported taxa**
- Chordata: Mammalia, Sauropsida, Actinopterygii (ray-finned fishes), other Vertebrates, Tunicates - Arthropoda: Hymenoptera, Diptera, Lepidoptera, Coleoptera, Hemiptera, Arachnida, other Arthropoda - Echinodermata, Mollusca, Cnidaria - Monocots (Liliopsida); Eudicots (Asterids, Rosids, Fabids, Caryophyllales)
.. class:: warningmark
Fungi, protists and nematodes are out of scope for EGAPx. Runs with an unsupported taxid will fail.
**Security notice**
EGAPx has dependencies that include several thousand files from the `NCBI C++ toolkit <https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/toolkit>`_ and more than a million lines of code. Static Application Security Testing has shown a small number of verified buffer overrun vulnerabilities. Consult your organizational security team regarding risks.

Resource requirements =====================
.. class:: warningmark
This tool runs the entire EGAPx Nextflow pipeline inside a single Galaxy job, so the job needs all of the resources the pipeline uses. The EGAPx README lists a machine with 32 CPUs and 256 GB RAM (or a cluster / AWS Batch) as a prerequisite. The job's Galaxy allocation (``GALAXY_SLOTS`` / ``GALAXY_MEMORY_MB``) is used to size the pipeline's processes, with a minimum of 4 CPUs and 6 GB; some steps (for example BUSCO) may still use all CPU cores visible to the job. A run can take many hours: NCBI reports that a 144 Mb fly genome with one short-read run took 71 CPU hours (3 hours wall clock on AWS Batch). This tool is not recommended for public servers.

Input =====
The required inputs are a genome assembly and an NCBI taxid (look it up on the `NCBI Taxonomy page <https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/taxonomy>`_). RNA-seq evidence is **highly recommended**.
**Genome**
- The genome does not need to be repeat-masked; EGAPx masks it as part of the pipeline. - Screen the assembly for contamination before annotating, for example with the NCBI `Foreign Contamination Screen <https://github.com/ncbi/fcs>`_. EGAPx fails with ``Too many protein hits to proks`` when too many gene models hit prokaryotes or viruses. - Keep organelle sequences in the FASTA to prevent inaccurate read mapping, but note that EGAPx does not annotate organelles. - Short, simple sequence names are less likely to cause problems.

**RNA-seq reads**
In the tool form, short and/or long reads can be selected from the history (FASTQ or FASTA, optionally gzipped), or typed in as a list of remote URLs and/or SRA run accessions. Reads from individual sequencing runs should be provided as separate files, never combined. Long reads must be FASTA or FASTQ, not BAM. An SRA Entrez query cannot be typed into the read list (it is split into separate words); supply it in a YAML configuration or the *Additional yaml* field instead.
.. class:: warningmark
An SRA Entrez query can match a very large number of runs, and the compute cost of a mistyped query or accession is potentially enormous. Run the query at the `NCBI SRA page <https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sra>`_ first and list a few runs explicitly if it returns too many. EGAPx refuses queries that return more runs than the **SRA query limit** (default 20, in *Developer options*).
**Proteins and noncoding RNAs**
- ``miniprot`` is the default protein aligner. ``ProSplign`` is slightly more accurate but more expensive, and may help when little RNA-seq evidence is available. - The protein evidence set is chosen from the taxid. You can change the number of organisms used, add extra proteins, or exclude taxids. NCBI recommends keeping the default set. - No noncoding RNAs are predicted by default. Enable ``cmsearch`` to predict rRNAs, snoRNAs and snRNAs from `Rfam <https://rfam.org/>`_, and ``tRNAscan`` to predict tRNAs.

YAML configuration ==================
An EGAPx run can be described by a YAML configuration from your history. Sample files are in the `EGAPx examples directory <https://github.com/ncbi/egapx/tree/v1.0.1/examples>`_. In a YAML configuration, the genome, reads and protein files must be given as URLs or SRA accessions/queries: history datasets and files on your own computer cannot be referenced. An excerpt of the small test example ``input_D_farinae_small.yaml``::
genome: https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/genomes/all/GCA/020/809/275/GCA_020809275.1_ASM2080927v1/GCA_020809275.1_ASM2080927v1_genomic.fna.gz taxid: 6954 short_reads: - - SRR8506572 - - https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/genomes/TOOLS/EGAP/sample_data/Dermatophagoides_farinae_small/SRR8506572.1 - https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/genomes/TOOLS/EGAP/sample_data/Dermatophagoides_farinae_small/SRR8506572.2 - - SRR9005248 - - https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/genomes/TOOLS/EGAP/sample_data/Dermatophagoides_farinae_small/SRR9005248.1 - https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/genomes/TOOLS/EGAP/sample_data/Dermatophagoides_farinae_small/SRR9005248.2 locus_tag_prefix: egapxtmp
Reads can also be a list of SRA runs::
short_reads: - SRR8506572 - SRR9005248
or an SRA Entrez query (``long_reads`` takes the same forms)::
short_reads: txid43150[Organism] AND 50:350[ReadLength] AND (illumina[Platform] OR bgiseq[Platform]) AND biomol_rna[Properties] long_reads: txid43150[Organism] AND (oxford_nanopore[Platform] OR pacbio_smrt[Platform]) AND biomol_rna[Properties]
Protein and noncoding RNA options::
protein_aligner_name: prosplign proteins_best_n_orgs: 5 proteins_deny_taxids: - 7227 trnascan: enabled: true cmsearch: enabled: true
Default task parameters can be overridden with a ``tasks:`` section (see ``ui/assets/default_task_params.yaml`` in the EGAPx repository). For example, to relax alignment criteria when using RNA-seq from a different species::
tasks: rnaseq_collapse: rnaseq_collapse: -high-identity 0.8 convert_from_bam: sam2asn: -filter 'pct_identity_gap >= 85' star_wnode: star_wnode: -pct-identity 85 max_intron: 700000 # otherwise calculated automatically

Output ======
- **Final annotation** (``complete.genomic.gff``): the final annotation set in GFF3 format. - **EGAPx output** collection:
============================== =========================================================================== Element Description ============================== =========================================================================== annotated_genome Final annotation set in ASN.1 format (input for GenBank submission) complete_genomic_gtf Final annotation set in GTF format complete_genomic_fna Full genome sequences in FASTA format complete_cds Annotated coding sequences (CDS) in FASTA format complete_transcripts Annotated transcripts, including UTRs, in FASTA format complete_proteins Annotated protein products in FASTA format annotation_data Annotation structured comment, used for GenBank submission sra_metadata Metadata for the SRA runs used gnomon_contam_rpt Gnomon contamination report gnomon_report Evidence supporting each Gnomon transcript model gnomon_quality_report Per-model summary of supporting evidence busco_report BUSCO short summary (text); empty if BUSCO failed busco_report_json BUSCO short summary (JSON); empty if BUSCO failed stats_feature_counts Feature counts by model prediction category stats_feature_stats Transcript, exon and feature length statistics stats_mask_assm_stats Genome masking statistics stats_prot_align_stats Protein alignment statistics validated_all_unannotated Validation warnings and errors (unannotated sequences) validated_genome Validation warnings and errors for annotated features ============================== ===========================================================================
- **EGAPx nextflow stats** collection: ``nextflow.log``, the Nextflow HTML execution report and timeline, the trace file (runtime and CPU use per process), and ``run_params.yaml`` (all parameters used). - **EGAPx MultiQC report** collection: the MultiQC HTML report and its data files. - **EGAPx RNA-seq alignment stats** collection: short-read (``rnaseq_short/``) and long-read (``rnaseq_long/``) alignment reports and statistics; empty when no reads of that type were used. - **EGAPx filtered protein alignments**: the protein alignments (ASN.1) passed to Gnomon, only when *Collect filtered protein alignments* is set in *Developer options*. - **EGAPx STAR alignments** collection: the STAR BAM files, only when *Collect BAM output from STAR* is set in *Developer options*.
Interpreting the output =======================
**MultiQC report**: one HTML report with feature counts and length statistics, BUSCO scores, genome masking statistics, and RNA-seq and protein alignment statistics. Alignment information for RNA-seq or proteins supplied as local data may currently be inaccurate or missing (see the `EGAPx release notes <https://github.com/ncbi/egapx/releases>`_).
**Feature counts**: summary counts are printed near the end of the job's standard output and are also in *stats_feature_counts*. Counts of protein-coding genes should be compared with similar species. Low counts may mean insufficient evidence; high counts may mean genome fragmentation, uncollapsed haplotypes, or genes annotated on transposons.
.. class:: warningmark
Genes with a ``major correction`` are likely protein-coding genes with frameshifts and/or internal stops. They have "LOW QUALITY PROTEIN" in the protein FASTA title and are adjusted to meet GenBank criteria. RefSeq releases an annotation only if no more than 10% of protein-coding genes have major corrections; polish the assembly if the rate is higher.
**BUSCO**: run in proteins mode on the longest isoform per gene, using the lineage chosen from the taxid. A BUSCO failure does not fail the job; the BUSCO reports are then empty. Low scores can indicate assembly problems, or an organism divergent from those used to build the BUSCO models. Expected BUSCO content for related organisms can be found on `NCBI Datasets <https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/datasets/genome/>`_.
**Contamination report** (*gnomon_contam_rpt*): per-sequence counts of gene models, single-exon models, and models whose best hit is to prokaryotes or viruses. Look for longer contigs with a high fraction of prokaryote hits, especially single-exon models; for example, sequences with at least 10 models where at least 50% hit prokaryotes or viruses.
**Gnomon reports**: *gnomon_report* lists each line of evidence (protein, long-read, short-read, *ab initio*) supporting each transcript model, and *gnomon_quality_report* summarizes the evidence per model. The best models have no *ab initio* contribution, high RNA-seq coverage, and few alignments needed for the minimal intron set. Column descriptions are in the `EGAPx README <https://github.com/ncbi/egapx/blob/v1.0.1/README.md#interpreting-output>`_.
**Troubleshooting**: if a run fails, the job's standard output and ``nextflow.log`` name the failing process. ``run.trace.txt`` lists every process with its status and resource use.
Submitting annotation to NCBI =============================
The *annotated_genome* ASN.1 output can be prepared for GenBank submission with the ``prepare_submission`` program from the EGAPx container (it is not run by this tool). You will need a submission template and BioProject/BioSample identifiers, and for a new assembly a registered locus_tag prefix. The prefix can be set when annotating (the *Locus tag prefix* form field or the ``locus_tag_prefix:`` YAML key) or passed to ``prepare_submission``. See `Submitting EGAPx annotation to NCBI <https://github.com/ncbi/egapx/blob/v1.0.1/README.md#submitting-egapx-annotation-to-ncbi>`_.

More information ================
See the `EGAPx repository <https://github.com/ncbi/egapx>`_ for full documentation and FAQ. Report problems with EGAPx itself at the `EGAPx issue tracker <https://github.com/ncbi/egapx/issues>`_, and problems with this Galaxy wrapper at the `wrapper repository <https://github.com/richard-burhans/galaxytools/issues>`_.
